fields.meta_title: Advertorial Landing Page Builder and Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Four advertorial landing page examples built from a prompt: a founder story, a listicle, a headline test, and a quote form, with what each counted.
fields.h1: Build an Advertorial Landing Page That Reads Like an Article
fields.hero_description: Build an advertorial landing page with an Advertisement label and tagged buy buttons, and save each click to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into an Advertorial
fields.features_subheading: From one description of the product and its reader, Emergent writes the article and the table that counts its clicks.
fields.feature_1:
An article drafted from your notes

Paste the founder's notes or a product brief, and Emergent drafts the page as an article under a headline and a byline, with spots for photos. Ask for any change by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A label set above the headline

Write the label once, such as Advertisement or Paid Advertisement, and ask for it above the headline in the byline's type. Every headline version of the page carries the same label.
fields.feature_3:
A tag on every buy button

Name each button by its spot in the article, such as intro or end. Each click is saved as a row in a database you own, with the tag, the time, and the headline version it came from.
fields.feature_4:
Headline versions with their own links

Ask for a second headline, and Emergent builds it as a version of the same page with its own link for a second ad. The table counts visitors and clicks for each version.
fields.feature_5:
A form at the end, an email to the rep

End the article with a short form in place of a buy button. Each request lands in your table, and the app emails the person you name when an answer matches a rule you set.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Paid plans include full code export of the page and its table to your GitHub repository. Or publish on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

fields.tab_content_1:
Under the Advertisement label, three buttons that count

Hushmoor's founder tested six weighted blankets before making her own, and the advertorial tells it under an Advertisement label. Three buy buttons in the article are tagged intro, middle, and end. Last week they sent 1,240 readers to the shop: 690 from the end button, 380 from the middle, and 170 from the intro.
fields.tab_content_2:
By reason, the cost per meal drew the most clicks

Pebblefoot lists seven reasons dog owners switch to fresh food, and each reason ends with a link tagged with its number. Reason 4 sets the cost per meal next to kibble. It drew 342 of the month's 900 clicks to the shop, more than any other reason on the list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two headlines, 2,000 visitors each

Dellwyn Filters wrote two headlines for one advertorial and gave each ad its own version of the page. One asks whether your tap water is safe; the other has a plumber explain what your filter misses. After 2,000 visitors each, the plumber's version sent 264 readers to the shop and the safety question sent 180.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every order of 8 windows or more goes to Ilse Navarro

Glasswick Windows tells how neighbors on Alder Street replaced drafty windows, and the article ends in a quote form asking for a ZIP code, the number of windows, and an email. When a request is for 8 windows or more, the app emails Ilse Navarro, the sales rep. That was 21 of last week's 58 requests.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Advertorial Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take an advertorial landing page from a product and a story to a labeled page that counts every click.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose one product and one reader
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the headline an editor would
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the label above the headline
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set proof next to each claim
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose one product and the reader it fits, such as a light sleeper who runs hot at night. An advertorial is a story about one person's problem, and a page written for everyone has no story to tell. Note the one claim the article has to prove.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Promise a story or a finding in the headline, such as I tested six blankets before making my own. Leave the brand name and the price out of it. Draft two or three versions, because the headline is the first thing worth testing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The FTC's native advertising guide asks for disclosures placed immediately in front of or above a native ad's headline. It lists Ad and Advertisement among the terms people understand, and it tells advertisers not to use terms such as Promoted.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Place the evidence for each product claim beside it: a photo from the test, a customer quote with a first name, a number with its source. Cut any claim you cannot back up on the page, however well it reads in the draft.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the article in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the product and the story, and say where each button sits. Emergent builds the copy and a click table, and the app tags every button. Send another prompt later to rewrite a paragraph or add a second headline.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before the ads go live, open the page from each ad's link and click every button once. Check that each click lands as a row with the right tag and headline version, and that each button opens the right product page.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the clicks after a week
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the first week, sort the clicks by button and by headline version. Move the wording of the strongest button into the weaker spots, retire the losing headline, and put the ad budget behind the version that sent more readers to the shop.

faq_plan.q: What is an advertorial landing page?
faq_plan.a: An advertorial landing page is a page written like an article that sells one product. Mailchimp defines an advertorial as a form of advertising that is designed to look like an editorial feature in a publication. The page sits between the ad and the product page: the story comes first, then the link to the shop.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an advertorial landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the product and the story in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It writes the article, sets your label above the headline, and adds a tag to each buy button. Change any section with another prompt, then publish the page and point your ads at it.

faq_plan.q: How long should an advertorial landing page be?
faq_plan.a: Long enough to tell one story and prove one claim, and no longer. Keep the paragraphs short, and cut any section that does not move the reader toward the product. Place the first buy button after the problem is clear, never in the opening paragraph.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between an advertorial landing page and a regular landing page?
faq_plan.a: An advertorial reads like an editorial story and sends the reader on to a product page, while a regular landing page sells directly. An artist landing page, for example, puts the music and the signup form right at the top. An advertorial earns the click with the story first.

faq_plan.q: Does an advertorial landing page need its own ad label if the ad already has one?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in the FTC's view, when the page looks like an article. Its native advertising guide says disclosures are needed both on the publisher's site and the click- or tap-into page on which the complete ad appears, unless the click-into page is obviously an ad.

faq_plan.q: How many buy buttons go on an advertorial landing page?
faq_plan.a: Start with three: one after the problem is set up, one in the middle of the story, and one at the end. Tag each one, and after a week cut the button that draws the fewest clicks. On Emergent, those counts sit in a database you own, next to the time of each click.

faq_plan.q: Can an advertorial landing page collect leads instead of sending readers to a store?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Swap the last buy button for a short quote request, such as ZIP code, number of windows, and email. If the offer is a free guide and not a quote, a lead magnet landing page may suit it better than a story. The app can email your rep when a request matches a rule you set.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which ad sent a reader to my advertorial landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give each ad its own link to the page, with a tag in the link such as ad=plumber. Ask Emergent to save that tag with every click and form request, and the table shows visitors and clicks for each ad side by side.

faq_plan.q: What does an advertorial landing page template include?
faq_plan.a: The layout, and little of what sells. A template sets the columns and the type, but the story does the selling, and no template writes it for your product. Emergent builds the page from a prompt, with no sample copy to strip out first.

faq_plan.q: Do advertorial landing pages work for local service businesses?
faq_plan.a: They can, when the service has a story worth reading, such as neighbors on one street who replaced old windows. For a service people search when they need it now, a direct roofing landing page with a quote form gets to the point faster. Run both when the budget allows, and compare the requests.

plan.angle: Searchers for an advertorial landing page are paid-social and native-ad marketers who want to see what one looks like and get one live: the results are template galleries, a glossary definition and example roundups that stop at screenshots. This page shows four advertorials built from a prompt and what each one records: a founder story with three tagged buttons, a listicle that counts clicks by reason, two headline versions split by ad, and a lead-gen article that ends in a quote form whose bigger requests go to one rep. It also covers the part the roundups skip: the Advertisement label above the headline, placed where the FTC's native advertising guide asks.
